n057aa66e9ea.s: The Central Administrative Tribunal is NOT bound by the:
n057aa66e9ea.x: CAT is not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure; it follows natural justice, charges nominal fees and lets parties appear in person.

nindian-polity-72-4.s: Tribunals in India are best described as:
nindian-polity-72-4.x: Tribunals are quasi-judicial bodies set up to reduce pendency in regular courts and bring domain expertise.

nindian-polity-72-43.s: Which Part of the Constitution deals with relations between the Union and the States?
nindian-polity-72-43.x: Part XI deals with Union-State relations; Part X deals with Scheduled and Tribal Areas and Part XIV-A with tribunals.

nindian-polity-72-12.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT)?
o: It has original jurisdiction over service matters of Union civil servants
Appeals against its orders go first to a High Court Division Bench
It derives its basis from Article 323A
Appeals against its orders lie directly before the Supreme Court
nindian-polity-72-12.x: Appeals against CAT orders go first to a Division Bench of the High Court, not straight to the Supreme Court.

nf33918363cd.s: Administrative Members of the Central Administrative Tribunal must have served at the level of:
nf33918363cd.x: Administrative Members need service at the level of Additional Secretary or above; Judicial Members must be qualified as High Court judges.

ncd67e73df9a.s: Of the 69 members of the Central Administrative Tribunal, how many are Judicial Members (including the Chairperson)?
ncd67e73df9a.x: CAT has 69 members: 35 Judicial Members, including the Chairperson, and 34 Administrative Members.

n8689fc24153.s: After the Madras Bar Association ruling of November 2025, the Search-cum-Selection Committee sends how many names per vacancy?
n8689fc24153.x: The ruling struck down the two-name arrangement; the committee now sends one name per vacancy.

nindian-polity-51-22.s: Constitutional amendments are tested in judicial review on the touchstone of the:
nindian-polity-51-22.x: Constitutional amendments are subject to judicial review and are tested against the basic structure doctrine.

n6b501d4a608.s: Under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, members of the National Tribunals Commission hold office for:
o: Five years or until 70, whichever is earlier
Five years or until 67, whichever is earlier
Three years or until 65, whichever is earlier
n6b501d4a608.x: The proposed tenure is five years or until the age of 70 years, whichever is earlier.

n164c3ac7af3.s: Under the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021, the minimum age for appointment as a tribunal member was:
n164c3ac7af3.x: The 2021 framework fixed a minimum appointment age of 50, a four-year tenure, and maximum ages of 70 (Chairperson) and 67 (members).

ndd6f3f5b501.s: Under the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, the Chairperson of the National Tribunals Commission may be a former Supreme Court judge or a former:
o: Chief Justice of a High Court
ndd6f3f5b501.x: The Chairperson may be a former Supreme Court judge or a former High Court Chief Justice; a serving SC judge is not required.

nba9530bc70d.s: In which country does Parliament hold all law-making power, reflecting a unitary system?
nba9530bc70d.x: The United Kingdom is unitary: its Parliament holds all law-making power. USA, Canada and Australia are federal.

nindian-polity-51-15.s: Which of the following reinforces the federal principle of the Indian Constitution?
nindian-polity-51-15.x: Judicial review upholds the division of powers and so supports federalism; emergency provisions, All India Services and single citizenship are unitary features.

n7ffe93491de.s: Who described Indian federalism as 'cooperative federalism'?
n7ffe93491de.x: Granville Austin called it cooperative federalism; Ivor Jennings called India a federation with a strong centralising tendency.

nc35d5076d4b.s: A loose league of sovereign States that keep the right to secede is called a:
nc35d5076d4b.x: A confederation is a loose league of sovereign States that generally keep the right to secede; a federation has a constitutional division of powers.

nf9272df3ac7.s: Which case held that the Indian Constitution is not truly federal and that the States are not sovereign?
o: Kesavananda Bharati v State of Kerala
S. R. Bommai v Union of India
Minerva Mills v Union of India
State of West Bengal v Union of India
nf9272df3ac7.x: In State of West Bengal v Union of India (1962) the Supreme Court held that States are not sovereign; it also upheld Parliament's power to acquire State property.

n97e788ef497.s: Which of the following had a separate constitution of its own?
o: Former State of Jammu and Kashmir
n97e788ef497.x: Indian States generally have no separate constitutions; the former Jammu and Kashmir was the exception. Each US State has its own.

nindian-polity-68-18.s: Land revenue is a subject in the:
nindian-polity-68-18.x: Land revenue is in the State List, while corporation tax is in the Union List.

nindian-polity-68-29.s: Public order, which the 42nd Amendment did not transfer, is placed in the:
nindian-polity-68-29.x: Public order remains State List Entry 1; the 42nd Amendment moved education, forests, weights and measures, wild animals and birds, and administration of justice.

nindian-polity-68-43.s: Public health and sanitation is a subject in the:
nindian-polity-68-43.x: Public health and sanitation is a State List subject, not a Concurrent one.

n4a3a5fb059e.s: Which Article gives Parliament exclusive power to legislate on matters not in the State List or the Concurrent List?
n4a3a5fb059e.x: Article 248 contains the residuary legislative power, including residuary taxes.

n6ff40310948.s: The 'administration of justice' entry moved to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Amendment covers:
o: Courts other than the Supreme Court and High Courts
The Supreme Court and High Courts
n6ff40310948.x: The entry moved covers courts other than the Supreme Court and High Courts; the 42nd Amendment moved five subjects in all.

ne857c7ecba1.s: Which of the following can happen during a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
o: Union automatically takes over State legislative powers
State Money Bills reserved for the President
Lok Sabha term extended by one year
ne857c7ecba1.x: Article 360 allows directions on State finances, salary cuts and reservation of State Money Bills; it does not transfer State legislative powers or suspend Fundamental Rights.

nindian-polity-50-48.s: Which emergency directly affects Fundamental Rights?
o: Both President's Rule and Financial Emergency
nindian-polity-50-48.x: Only a National Emergency affects Fundamental Rights (Articles 358 and 359); President's Rule and Financial Emergency do not.

nindian-polity-68-19.s: Which Article empowers both Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws on GST?
nindian-polity-68-19.x: Article 246A gives Parliament and State Legislatures simultaneous power over GST; Panchayati Raj stays a State List subject.

n7d399f145ba.s: Under Article 252, Parliament may legislate on a State List subject when resolutions are passed by:
n7d399f145ba.x: Article 252 needs resolutions of the legislatures of two or more States; one State is not enough.

nindian-polity-2-50.s: The Inter-State Council is provided for in Article:
nindian-polity-2-50.x: Articles 256-263 deal with administrative relations, ending with Article 263 on the Inter-State Council.

nindian-polity-2-51.s: Article 281 of the Constitution deals with:
nindian-polity-2-51.x: Article 281 deals with the Finance Commission's recommendations; the Commission itself is constituted under Article 280.

nindian-polity-67-8.s: Which doctrine looks at the true nature of a law and ignores its incidental encroachment on another List?
nindian-polity-67-8.x: The doctrine of pith and substance resolves overlaps between the Lists by examining the law's true nature.

nindian-polity-67-28.s: The Doctrine of Eclipse is associated with which case?
o: Prafulla Kumar v Bank of Commerce
Bhikaji Narain Dhakras v State of M.P.
Kameshwar Singh v State of Bihar
A.K. Gopalan v State of Madras
nindian-polity-67-28.x: The Doctrine of Eclipse comes from Bhikaji Narain Dhakras; Prafulla Kumar is a pith and substance case.

new.s: Part XIV-A (Articles 323-A and 323-B) was inserted on the advice of the:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment, 1976 inserted Part XIV-A on the Swaran Singh Committee's advice.

new.s: Which Amendment added the rent and tenancy clause to Article 323-B?
new.x: The 75th Amendment, 1994 added clause (h) on rent and tenancy to Article 323-B.

new.s: Which Article allows a hierarchy of tribunals (original and appellate)?
new.x: Article 323-B allows a hierarchy of tribunals; under Article 323-A there is one CAT plus State tribunals with no hierarchy.

new.s: A major criticism of tribunals is that they are:
o: Bound by the full Code of Civil Procedure
Run by the ministries whose decisions they review
new.x: Tribunals are criticised as being run by the same ministries whose decisions they review; low cost, expertise and freedom from the CPC are their merits.

new.s: The first tribunal set up under Article 323A was the:
new.x: The CAT, set up in 1985 under the Administrative Tribunals Act, was the first tribunal under Article 323A.

new.s: The Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal was abolished in:
new.x: The Centre's notification of 14 January 2020 abolished APAT; in 2016 Telangana was removed from its jurisdiction and in 1989 it was reconstituted.

new.s: The AP Administrative Tribunal was constituted by a Presidential order of 19 May 1975 under Article:
new.x: APAT was constituted under Article 371D(3), inserted by the 32nd Amendment, 1973.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Andhra Pradesh Administrative Tribunal:
1. It started working from 6 July 1976.
2. Telangana was removed from its jurisdiction in 2016.
3. After its abolition, its service cases went to the Central Administrative Tribunal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: APAT worked from 6 July 1976 and lost Telangana in 2016; after abolition its cases went to the AP High Court, not the CAT.

new.s: The Armed Forces Tribunal was set up under the AFT Act of:
new.x: The Armed Forces Tribunal Act was passed in 2007; 2010 is the NGT Act, 2013 the Companies Act and 1993 the debt recovery law.

new.s: Which of the following cities does NOT have a bench of the Armed Forces Tribunal?
new.x: AFT has regional benches at Jaipur, Jabalpur and Guwahati but none at Bhopal (APPSC GS 2024).

new.s: CESTAT hears disputes relating to:
new.x: CESTAT, under the Customs Act, 1962, deals with customs, excise and service tax.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Armed Forces Tribunal – Recovery of Debts and Bankruptcy Act, 1993
new.x: CESTAT works under the Customs Act, 1962; DRTs come under the 1993 debt recovery law, TDSAT under the TRAI law and AFT under its 2007 Act.

new.s: The Vansadhara Water Disputes Tribunal, relevant to Andhra Pradesh, was set up in:
new.x: AP water tribunals under Article 262: Godavari 1969, Krishna-II 2004 and Vansadhara 2010.

new.s: Which of the following cities has a zonal bench of the National Green Tribunal?
new.x: NGT's zonal benches are Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai, with the principal bench at New Delhi.

new.s: Under Section 20 of the NGT Act, the Tribunal applies sustainable development, the precautionary principle and the:
new.x: Section 20 directs the NGT to apply sustainable development, the precautionary principle and polluter pays.

new.s: The National Green Tribunal gives effect to the right to a healthy environment read into Article:
new.x: The NGT gives effect to the right to a healthy environment, which is read into Article 21.

new.s: Which case held that tribunals could replace High Courts as an effective substitute?
new.x: S.P. Sampath Kumar (1987) let tribunals replace High Courts; L. Chandra Kumar (1997) overruled it, holding that tribunals only supplement them.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT abolished by the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021?
new.x: The 2021 Act abolished FCAT, IPAB, the Airport Appellate Tribunal, AAR (Customs) and the Plant Varieties appellate tribunal; the NGT continues.

new.s: How many members, including the Chairperson, is the proposed National Tribunals Commission to have?
new.x: The NTC is to have five members: the Chairperson, two judicial and two technical members.

new.s: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026 was moved in Parliament by Law Minister:
new.x: Law Minister Arjun Ram Meghwal moved the Bill, which repeals the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021.

new.s: Which of the following countries is unitary?
new.x: Sri Lanka is unitary; Canada, Australia and Argentina are federal.

new.s: The federal scheme of the Indian Constitution was mainly taken from the:
new.x: The federal scheme, the office of Governor and the emergency provisions come from the Government of India Act, 1935.

new.s: India, Spain and Belgium are examples of:
new.x: In a holding-together federation a large country divides power to hold its diversity, as in India, Spain and Belgium.

new.s: India is described as an indestructible Union of:
new.x: Since States have no territorial guarantee (Article 3), India is an indestructible Union of destructible States; the USA's States are indestructible.

new.s: The Governor of a State is appointed by the Centre under Articles:
new.x: Articles 155-156 provide for the Governor's appointment by the Centre, a unitary feature.

new.s: Amendment of the federal provisions of the Constitution needs ratification by:
new.x: Most provisions are amended by Parliament alone, but federal provisions also need ratification by half the States (Article 368).

new.s:
Consider the following statements about features of the Indian Constitution:
1. Single citizenship is a unitary feature.
2. An integrated judiciary is a federal feature.
3. Bicameralism is a federal feature.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Single citizenship and an integrated judiciary are unitary features, while bicameralism is federal, so 2 is wrong.

new.s: 'Bargaining federalism' is associated with:
new.x: Morris-Jones called it bargaining federalism; Austin's label is cooperative federalism.

new.s: Who described the Indian system as 'extremely federal'?
new.x: Paul Appleby called it extremely federal; Wheare called it quasi-federal.

new.s: Who called the emergency powers a 'fraud on the Constitution'?
new.x: K.M. Nambiar called the emergency powers a fraud on the Constitution; H.V. Kamath used 'elephantine size'.

new.s: How many entries does the State List have now?
new.x: The State List has 59 entries now, against 66 originally; the Concurrent List now has 52.

new.s: Railway Police is a subject in the:
new.x: Railways are a Union subject but Railway Police is a State List subject.

new.s: Water is placed in the State List at Entry:
new.x: Water is State Entry 17; agriculture is Entry 14, land Entry 18 and taxes on mineral rights Entry 50.

new.s: Taxes on mineral rights fall under:
new.x: Taxes on mineral rights are State Entry 50; Union 85 is corporation tax, Concurrent 20 economic planning and State 45 land revenue.

new.s: Under the Government of India Act, 1935, residuary powers were vested in the:
new.x: The 1935 Act gave residuary powers to the Governor-General; India and Canada now give them to the Centre.

new.s: Which of the following is a residuary tax?
new.x: Gift, wealth and expenditure taxes are residuary taxes under Article 248; the others are listed in the Union or State List.

new.s: How many subjects did the 42nd Amendment, 1976 move from the State List to the Concurrent List?
new.x: Five subjects moved: education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice.

new.s: During a National Emergency, Parliament may extend the term of the Lok Sabha by:
new.x: Parliament may extend Lok Sabha and Assembly terms by one year at a time, up to six months after the Emergency ends.

new.s: The maximum duration of President's Rule under Article 356 is:
new.x: President's Rule runs six months at a time up to three years; a National Emergency has no maximum.

new.s: How many times has a Financial Emergency under Article 360 been proclaimed?
new.x: Financial Emergency has never been declared; National Emergency was proclaimed three times (1962, 1971, 1975).

new.s: A special Lok Sabha sitting to disapprove a National Emergency can be sought by a notice signed by:
new.x: The 44th Amendment lets one-tenth of Lok Sabha members seek a sitting within 14 days to disapprove the Emergency.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Article 253 – Laws to implement international agreements
Article 250 – Request of two or more States
new.x: Article 253 covers treaties; 250 is National Emergency, 252 the request of two or more States and 249 the Rajya Sabha resolution.

new.s: In the US Senate, each State is represented by:
new.x: The US Senate gives two seats to every State; Rajya Sabha seats are broadly by population.

new.s: Which of the following is found in India but not in the USA?
new.x: India has single citizenship while the USA has dual; a written Constitution, division of powers and a federal Supreme Court are common to both.

new.s: Article 371A makes special provisions for:
new.x: Article 371A is for Nagaland; 371F is Sikkim, 371J Karnataka and 371D Andhra Pradesh.

new.s: The Sarkaria Commission on Centre-State relations was set up in:
new.x: The Sarkaria Commission came in 1983; 1969 is the Rajamannar Committee and 1990 the Inter-State Council.

new.s: Which committee, set up by Tamil Nadu, gave a Part 1 report on Union-State relations in February 2026?
new.x: The Justice Kurian Joseph High-Level Committee of Tamil Nadu gave its Part 1 report in February 2026.

new.s: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse (Articles 301-307) is in Part:
new.x: Articles 301-307 form Part XIII; Part XI covers Union-State relations.

new.s: Parliament may set up additional courts for the better administration of Union laws under Article:
new.x: Article 247 allows additional courts for Union laws; 248 is residuary power, 251 inconsistency and 255 procedure.

new.s: Laws with extra-territorial operation can be made by:
new.x: Only Parliament can make extra-territorial laws (Article 245(2)); a State law needs a territorial nexus.

new.s: A State law may reach outside the State only when there is a:
new.x: A State legislature makes laws for its own State; outside reach is valid only with a real territorial nexus.

new.s: Entries 52 and 55 of the State List were omitted by the:
new.x: The 101st Amendment (GST) omitted State Entries 52 and 55; the 42nd omitted 11, 19, 20, 29 and the 7th omitted 36.

new.s: Article 246(3) gives State Legislatures exclusive power over the:
new.x: Under Article 246(3) States have exclusive power over List II, subject to clauses (1) and (2).

new.s: Which of the following is NOT in the Union List?
new.x: Agriculture is State Entry 14; RBI, foreign loans and census are Union subjects.

new.s: Adulteration of foodstuffs falls in the:
new.x: Adulteration of foodstuffs, drugs and electricity are Concurrent List subjects.

new.s: Elections to the State Legislature are in the State List at Entry:
new.x: State Entry 37 covers elections to the State Legislature; 45 is land revenue, 50 mineral-right taxes and 26 intra-State trade.

new.s: Forests were moved from the State List to the Concurrent List by the:
new.x: The 42nd Amendment moved forests and education, among others, from the State List to the Concurrent List.

new.s: Which of the following falls under Parliament's residuary power?
new.x: Space research, cyber law and residuary taxation are residuary subjects; police is State, education Concurrent and railways Union.

new.s: In Canada, residuary powers lie with the:
new.x: India and Canada vest residuary powers in the Centre; the USA and Australia vest them in the States.

new.s: The Prize Competition Act, the first law in the Article 252 list, was passed in:
new.x: The Prize Competition Act, 1955 came first; the Wild Life Act (1972), Water Act (1974) and Urban Land Ceiling Act (1976) followed.

new.s: K.C. Gajapati Narayan Deo v State of Orissa (1953) is linked with the Doctrine of:
new.x: Gajapati Narayan Deo and Kameshwar Singh are colourable legislation cases: what cannot be done directly cannot be done indirectly.

new.s: Kerala said the MMDR (Amendment) Bill, 2026 enters State List Entries 18 and:
new.x: Kerala argued the Bill enters State Entry 18 (land) and Entry 50 (taxes on mineral rights).

new.s: States demand a review of Centre-State relations mainly because they:
new.x: States seek a review of Centre-State relations because they lack adequate resources.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the National Green Tribunal:
1. It was established on 18 October 2010.
2. It is bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: The NGT was established on 18.10.2010 under the NGT Act; it follows natural justice and is not bound by the CPC, 1908.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Article 249:
1. The resolution is passed by the Rajya Sabha by two-thirds of members present and voting.
2. The resolution remains in force for up to one year and can be renewed.
3. The Lok Sabha must also pass a concurring resolution.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Article 249 needs only a Rajya Sabha resolution by two-thirds present and voting, valid up to one year and renewable; the Lok Sabha takes no part.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT an effect of a National Emergency on the States?
o: The Union can direct any State on its executive power
The President may modify revenue distribution under Article 354
Parliament may extend Assembly terms by one year at a time
Parliament loses power over the State List
new.x: During a National Emergency Parliament gains power over the State List (Article 250); the other three are listed effects.
